# IMAGINE: placeholders and the asset list

What IMAGINE needs and how its characters and guns start out. The pipeline that builds every asset is a platform doc: [docs/CONTENT.md](../../../docs/CONTENT.md). Content lives in `games/imagine/content/`. Why placeholders: [decision index](../../../docs/README.md) D3.

## 1. Placeholder policy (now)

**Characters and guns are simple placeholders, generated by scripts, so gameplay and graphics work can start at once.** You will replace them with real models later. The **replacement contract** makes that a drop-in swap: keep the same object names, skeleton bone names, socket names, scale and origin, and re-export.

### 1.1 Placeholder characters (`tools/blender/make_characters.py`, run for this game)
- One shared skeleton (`rig_human`: 22 bones, standard names `hips`, `spine`, `chest`, `neck`, `head`, `shoulder_l/r`, `upper_arm_l/r`, `forearm_l/r`, `hand_l/r`, `thigh_l/r`, `shin_l/r`, `foot_l/r`, `toe_l/r`, `weapon_r`, `camera`).
- A **mannequin** made of simple rounded blocks, each block parented to one bone (rigid skinning, nothing stretches). It is clean, stylised and readable, not a grey capsule.
- Three builds from the same skeleton: **Light** (slim, 1.75 m), **Medium** (1.80 m, vest block), **Heavy** (1.85 m, wide shoulders, helmet block).
- A team-colour panel on the shoulders and back (≥ 8 % of the silhouette, [LOOK.md](LOOK.md)), driven by a material parameter.
- **First-person arms:** forearms and hands only, on the same skeleton.
- **Animations** keyed by script for a start: idle, walk, run, crouch, jump, slide, fire, reload, equip, death. Real animations replace them clip by clip.
- Hit-box shapes per bone (head, chest, limbs) exported as `_HIT` capsules.

### 1.1a Operator base body (sourced, 2026-11-12)

`content/characters/man_base/source/`: Grab3D "Man Base Mesh", **CC0 1.0** (`LICENSE.txt`, `manifest.json` committed beside it), downloaded from grab3d.com/models/characters/man-base-character/.
- `man-base-character-rigged.glb` (11 MB): rigged, with walk and run clips; 1.80 m, A-pose, T-shirt and shorts, bare feet; PBR textures.
- `man-base-character-light.glb` (4 MB): the static light version (131k triangles, 1K textures).
- **AI disclosure:** the licence file states the asset is AI-assisted (generated with Meshy, cleaned up in Blender). Stores that require disclosure of AI-generated content (for example Steam) must list it.
- It is a base body, not an operator. The operator look (armour, helmet, gloves, boots, team-colour panels per LOOK.md) is built over it by a Blender script, as the weapons are, and decimated for phones; the source stays unmodified.

### 1.2 Placeholder guns (`tools/blender/make_guns.py`)
Each gun is a few bevelled blocks and cylinders with a distinct silhouette, one clean material and the sockets `socket_grip`, `socket_muzzle`, `socket_eject`, `socket_sight`, `socket_mag`. The magazine is a separate object so reloads can move it.

| Gun | Role | Silhouette |
|---|---|---|
| Assault rifle | all-round (built first) | medium body, straight magazine, stock |
| SMG | close, fast | short body, long thin magazine, folded stock |
| Shotgun | very close, breaching | long tube, pump grip |
| Marksman rifle | long range | long barrel, scope block |
| LMG | hold an area, break cover | heavy body, box magazine, bipod |
| Pistol | backup | small block, grip |

The gameplay feel of a gun lives in its data file (damage, fire rate, recoil pattern, wall damage), not in the model, so guns can feel finished while still looking simple.

## 2. Asset list for launch

Season 1 = Survival Protocol, Control Shift, Practice, one arena, rifle, pistol and shotgun first ([PLAN.md](PLAN.md) §2, §9). The list below predates D51 and is revised at M3.

| Group | Items | Source now | Later |
|---|---|---|---|
| Characters | 3 builds + arms + hit boxes + ~10 clips | script placeholders (§1.1) | modelled in Blender by you; ~60 third-person clips |
| Guns | 6 | script placeholders (§1.2) | modelled by you |
| Gadgets | breach charge, smoke, barricade, heal, grapple, scanner | simple blocks | modelled |
| Kiln Yard kit | walls (concrete, brick, wood), floors, beams, columns, stairs, windows, doors, each in 2–3 pre-broken patterns | modelled in Blender (we build it; scripts generate the modular pieces) | detail pass |
| Props | crane, scaffolding, containers, explosive barrels, pallets, sandbags, cables, work lights | simple models | detail pass |
| Materials (~12) | concrete, brick, plaster, wood, steel, corrugated metal, glass, dirt, gravel, asphalt, plastic sheeting, rubber | free CC0 texture sets (Poly Haven), reworked to fit the art direction | custom |
| Sky | 1 HDR sky (daytime) for reflection reference; the game sky is procedural ([RENDERING.md](../../../docs/RENDERING.md) §14) | Poly Haven (CC0) | per season |
| Effects | gun set ([PRINCIPLES.md](../../../docs/PRINCIPLES.md) §5.3 checklist) × 6, destruction set × materials, explosions, smoke, fire, sparks | made in-house as effect files with flipbooks | — |
| Sounds | gun layers × 6, footsteps per surface, body movement, destruction stages per material, gadgets, UI family, ambience, 4 music cues | free CC0 libraries and our own recordings, or a paid library whose licence allows a sold game | custom |
| Fonts | Big Shoulders Display, Barlow, Barlow Condensed, JetBrains Mono (all OFL) | Google Fonts | — |
| Icons (~80) | guns, gadgets, team glyphs ▲●■◆, HUD symbols | drawn as SVG in one style | — |
